page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv5 family. It is equipped with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor, which operates at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The instance is configured with 256 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It includes a bundled 2458 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates strong multi-core processing capabilities, scoring in the top tier for multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Large-block memory read and write bandwidths also rank in the top 25%, facilitating rapid data transfer for memory-intensive operations. The hardware performs exceptionally well in database operations, static web serving throughput, and software compilation. Conversely, single-core performance and text processing benchmarks fall within the average range, and large-model LLM text generation represents a notable performance bottleneck.

From a resource density perspective, the D64ds_v5 offers a balanced allocation of compute, memory, and high-capacity local SSD storage. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high-throughput local disk access without the premium cost of memory-optimized instances. It is highly suitable for multi-threaded applications, relational databases, static web serving, software development pipelines, and moderate-scale data processing tasks.
